lessonTitle: On time vs In time (and At the end vs In the end)

gapFill.title: Fill in the gaps
gapFill.subtitle: Type on, in or at to complete on time / in time / at the end / in the end. Twenty original sentences.

questions.explain: At the scheduled time, punctual: on time. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.after: time for the exam. It starts at nine.
questions.explain: Punctual for a planned time: on time. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.
Never late: on time. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.
At the planned time: on time. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.
Early enough to do something: in time to. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.
Early enough for something: in time for. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.
Early enough to do something important: in time. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.before: Hurry, or we won’t be there
questions.explain: Early enough for the start: in time. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.
Fixed phrase: just in time = at the last moment. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.
The final point of a place: at the end of. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.after: the end of the film, everybody cried.
questions.explain: The final part of something: at the end of the film.
The final point of a period: at the end of. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.
The last part of a month: at the end of June. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.
Finally, after discussion: in the end. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.before: I looked at lots of phones and
questions.after: the end I bought the cheapest one.
questions.explain: Finally, after a long time: in the end. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.after: the end the match was cancelled.
questions.explain: The final result: in the end. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.after: the end the interview went well.
questions.explain: Finally: in the end (no ‘of’). On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.
‘At the end’ is usually followed by ‘of’ + noun. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.
‘In time for’ + noun: in time for the wedding. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.
‘In time to’ + verb: in time to say goodbye. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

timedMC.title: Beat the clock
timedMC.subtitle: 15 seconds per question. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = the final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: The concert started exactly at eight — right       .
wrongReasons: ‘In time’ means early enough for something, not punctual.
‘At the end’ refers to the final point of something.
‘In the end’ means finally, after a long time.
questions.explain: At the scheduled time: on time. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: We ran and got to the station        to catch the last train.
wrongReasons: ‘On time’ means punctual; here the point is early enough to catch it.
‘At the end’ needs ‘of’ and means the final point.
questions.explain: Early enough to do something: in time to. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: The answers are        of the book.
wrongReasons: ‘In the end of’ is a common mistake.
‘In time’ is about being early enough.
questions.explain: The final point of something: at the end of. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: We couldn’t decide for ages, but        we chose Italy.
wrongReasons: ‘At the end’ refers to a final point and usually needs ‘of’.
‘In time’ is about being early enough.
questions.explain: Finally, after a long time: in the end. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: I got home just        for the start of the match.
wrongReasons: ‘On time for the start’ is less natural: the idea is early enough.
questions.explain: Early enough for something: in time for. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: Trains in Switzerland are almost always       .
wrongReasons: ‘In time’ means early enough for something.
questions.explain: Punctual: on time. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: of the lesson, the teacher gave us homework.
wrongReasons: ‘By the end’ means not later than.
questions.explain: Final point of an event: at the end of. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: The car broke down twice, but        we got there.
wrongReasons: ‘At the end’ doesn’t mean finally here.
You were probably late, so not ‘on time’.
‘At the end of’ needs a noun.
questions.explain: Finally, after problems: in the end. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: The doctor arrived        to save his life.
wrongReasons: ‘At the end’ is a final point.
questions.explain: Early enough to do something: in time. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: We reached the gate        — they were closing it!
wrongReasons: ‘Just on time’ is less natural for the last moment.
‘Just at the end’ changes the meaning.
questions.explain: At the last possible moment: just in time. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: My cousins are coming        of August.
questions.explain: The last part of a month: at the end of. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: It was a difficult exam, but        I passed.
wrongReasons: ‘At the end’ means a final point, not ‘finally’.
‘At the end of’ needs a noun.
questions.explain: Finally: in the end. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: If you aren’t       , you can’t do the test.
wrongReasons: ‘At the end’ is a final point.
questions.explain: Punctual: on time. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: Which is correct?
choices: at the end of the film
in the end of the film
on the end of the film
questions.explain: at the end of + noun. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: We arrived in time        see the fireworks.
wrongReasons: ‘For’ is followed by a noun, not a verb.
questions.explain: ‘In time to’ + verb. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: Will you be home in time        dinner?
questions.explain: ‘In time for’ + noun. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: Which sentence means ‘finally’?
choices: In the end, we stayed in.
At the end of the day, we stayed in.
wrongReasons: That gives a time of day.
questions.explain: ‘In the end’ = finally. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: Which sentence means ‘punctual’?
choices: The bus arrived in time for us.
The bus arrived in the end.
The bus arrived at the end.
wrongReasons: That means early enough for us.
questions.explain: ‘On time’ = punctual. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: Turn right        of the road.
questions.explain: Final point of a place: at the end of. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.

questions.text: He didn’t want to come, but        he enjoyed it.
wrongReasons: ‘At the end’ means a final point.
questions.explain: Finally, after changing his mind: in the end. On time = punctual; in time = early enough; at the end of = final point; in the end = finally.
